notes: Direct HTTP fetch (Salesforce Commerce Cloud/Demandware SSR HTML), no proxy needed, consistent with the prior Furniture-pass access notes for SR25. robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (only generic Disallow for /search*, /cart*, /account*, /checkout*, and a few demandware.store AJAX endpoints under User-agent: *). Discovery: homepage main nav/mega-menu (top-level 'Best Sellers' link at /c/best-sellers/, plus a 'Best Sellers' sub-link inside every department's mega-menu column, e.g. 'Furniture Best Sellers', 'Gifts Best Sellers') cross-checked against sitemap_8-category.xml (12 confirmed *-best-sellers/ category URLs; a 13th, /c/holidays/christmas-shop/christmas-best-sellers/, is a stale sitemap entry that now 404s - seasonal page currently taken down out of season, excluded). Each page's own SSR grid header 'N Items' (input#ajax-js-search-count also carries the same number) was taken as qty; H1/breadcrumb on every page reads exactly '<X> Best Sellers' (Lighting's H1 is 'Top-Selling Lamps and Lighting Fixtures' but breadcrumb/nav label is 'Lighting Best Sellers'), confirming each is a genuine bestseller merchandising PLP, not a badge or editorial page. The top /c/best-sellers/ (733) is its own curated 'Shop All Best Sellers' listing and does not equal the sum of the 12 department pages (928) - expected, not an error (same pattern as parent/child count mismatches noted in the prior Home Decor pass for this site). Considered and EXCLUDED: /c/new-and-trending/trending/ (H1 'Trending Home Decor & Furniture', 1,332 items) - although 'Trending' is a Bestsellers target term, this page is a directory of unrelated themed micro-shops (Halloween, Harry Potter, Pizza Shop, Cat Shop, Sardine Shop, The Beaded Shop, Rifle Paper Co. x Loloi, etc.) rather than a ranked popularity/top-selling listing, so it reads as a marketing/collection hub, not a genuine Bestsellers-type PLP. No local-language search needed (US/English-only site). Site search itself was not queried directly since robots.txt disallows /search* for all crawlers and nav+sitemap already gave full, unambiguous coverage.
